# Diagnosing Memory Leaks in a Python HTTP Server During Long-Running Integration Tests

## 1. Pre-Test Setup & Baseline Establishment

### 1.1 Establish a Clean Baseline
```bash
# Record initial memory usage before starting the server
python3 -c "import resource; print(resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss)"

# Or use /proc for Linux
cat /proc/self/status | grep VmRSS

# Take a baseline snapshot with tracemalloc (insert at start of test suite)
import tracemalloc
tracemalloc.start(25)  # Track up to 25 frames deep
```

### 1.2 Enable Detailed Logging
```python
# In your server startup code
import logging
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format='%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(name)s: %(message)s')
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
```

### 1.3 Isolate the Test Environment
```bash
# Run in a clean virtual environment to rule out dependency issues
python3 -m venv leak_env
source leak_env/bin/activate
pip install --no-cache-dir your-package http-server-lib test-framework

# Disable unnecessary background processes
export PYTHONOPTIMIZE=0  # Don't strip docstrings (helps debugging)
export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
```

---

## 2. Memory Profiling & Monitoring

### 2.1 Real-Time Memory Monitoring During Tests

```bash
# Terminal 1: Start the server under test
python -m myserver --port 8080

# Terminal 2: Monitor memory in real time (Linux)
watch -n 1 "ps -o pid,rss,vsz,%mem,cmd -p $(pgrep -f 'myserver')"

# Terminal 3: Track RSS over time for graphing
while true; do
    echo "$(date +%s) $(cat /proc/$(pgrep -f 'myserver')/status | grep VmRSS | awk '{print $2}')" >> memory_trace.log
    sleep 5
done

# Terminal 4: Monitor file descriptors (common leak source)
watch -n 1 "ls -l /proc/$(pgrep -f 'myserver')/fd | wc -l"
```
